# Tako

> Tako is a data intelligence platform. The Tako MCP server lets AI agents search a proprietary, continuously-updated knowledge base of 100K+ curated charts — carrying the latest reported quarter, same-day market prices, and official releases as they publish, not static historical reference — get grounded answers, explore Tako's data graph, fetch underlying source content, and run a multi-step Answer Agent. It is a hosted remote MCP server on Cloudflare Workers.

## Documentation

- [MCP Server Setup](https://github.com/TakoData/tako-mcp): Connect to the hosted Tako MCP server
- [API Reference](https://tako.com/docs/): Full REST API documentation
- [Chart Gallery](https://tako.com/gallery): Browse example charts and visualizations
- [OpenAPI Spec](https://tako.com/openapi.yaml): Machine-readable API specification

## Connecting

Hosted endpoint: `https://mcp.tako.com/mcp` (Streamable HTTP).

- CLI/desktop hosts (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf): pass `Authorization: Bearer <TAKO_API_TOKEN>`. Get a token at tako.com -> account settings -> API tokens.
- Web hosts (Claude.ai, ChatGPT): connect via the server's OAuth flow; no token config needed.

Optional tools: some tools are opt-in and off by default, to keep the default surface small. Enable them by adding `?tools=` to the endpoint URL with comma-separated aliases, e.g. `https://mcp.tako.com/mcp?tools=agent,visualize`. Aliases: `agent` (Answer Agent — the server picks the single-call `tako_agent` on most clients and the `tako_agent_start` / `tako_agent_wait` pair on ChatGPT), `visualize` (`tako_visualize`; already on by default for ChatGPT, where it powers the chart widget), `graph_node` (`tako_graph_node`), `credits` (`get_credit_balance`). Only aliases are recognized (not raw tool names); unknown `?tools=` values are ignored, so a typo never breaks the connection.

Tools are discovered at runtime via `tools/list`. There is no per-call `api_token` argument — auth is connection-level.

## Available Tools

### Search vs. Answer — the core distinction

`tako_search` and `tako_answer` both read Tako's data graph and the live web, but return opposite things:

- **Want the DATA** — cards, rows, or a chart to work with or show? Use `tako_search`. It is fast and built to fan out: fire many narrow one-entity+one-metric queries in parallel and assemble the result yourself. The top card auto-renders as an interactive chart.
- **Want one written ANSWER** to a single, specific data question? Use `tako_answer`. It returns one synthesized answer grounded in the cards it cites.

Never send a broad or multi-part question to either tool as one call — split it into narrow entity+metric searches (e.g. "US CPI inflation", "US core CPI inflation", "US PCE inflation", "US core PCE inflation"). In one line: `tako_search` hands you the evidence, `tako_answer` hands you the conclusion. For open-ended, multi-step research use `tako_agent` (opt-in).

### tako_search
Fast, direct retrieval of a data point from Tako's data graph and the live web, returned as structured `cards` (each with a free preview of its latest rows) plus `web_results`; the top card auto-renders inline as an interactive chart. It replaces a generic web search for data lookups.

Built to fan out: each query should resolve one entity + one metric ("Apple revenue", "Nvidia vs AMD gross margin"), and many narrow queries fired in parallel retrieve far better than one broad or compound query. Listing what Tako covers is a `tako_graph_search` + `tako_graph_related` job, not a keyword search. Ground a query by pinning resolved graph ids. For a card's full rows call `tako_contents` — only when the card exposes a `content` attribute (non-null); without it the preview and chart are all there is. For one written answer use `tako_answer`; for open-ended research use `tako_agent` (opt-in).

Parameters:
- `query` (string, required): Natural-language query — one entity + one metric; parallelize multiple.
- `sources` (array): both by default (`["data","web"]`); pass `["data"]` for curated data only or `["web"]` for live web only. (`"tako"` is a legacy synonym for `"data"`.)
- `effort` (string, "fast" | "instant"): "fast" (default) or "instant" (fastest, cached embeds). Omit for fast.
- `count` (integer, 1-20, default 10): Maximum results per source.
- `include_contents` (boolean, default true): Inline each card's free row preview; set false for a pointers-only response (cheaper when fanning out many parallel queries). Full rows are always a separate `tako_contents` call.
- `country_code` (string, default "US"): ISO country code.
- `locale` (string, default "en-US"): Locale.
- `node_ids` (array of strings, max 20, optional): Graph node ids (from `tako_graph_search` / `tako_graph_related`, or a card's `nodes`) to PIN into the Tako data source — strong retrieval boost.
- `strict` (boolean, default false): Hard filter — when true, return ONLY cards matching at least one pinned node (requires non-empty `node_ids`).

### tako_answer
Ask one specific, self-contained data question; get one synthesized answer grounded in the `cards` it cites. It replaces a generic web search when you want the answer written out rather than a list of results. The `answer` is already synthesized from its citations. To work with the underlying data instead, or for a broad/multi-part question, use `tako_search` (parallelized into narrow entity+metric queries). To pull a cited card's rows, call `tako_contents` on its url (only when its `content` attribute is present).

Parameters:
- `query` (string, required): One specific, self-contained question.
- `sources` (array, optional): both by default (`["data","web"]`); pass `["data"]` for curated data only or `["web"]` for live web only. (`"tako"` is a legacy synonym for `"data"`.)
- `country_code` (string, default "US"): ISO country code.
- `locale` (string, default "en-US"): Locale.
- `node_ids` (array of strings, max 20, optional): Graph node ids to PIN into the Tako data source — strong retrieval boost.
- `strict` (boolean, default false): Hard filter — when true, return ONLY cards matching at least one pinned node (requires non-empty `node_ids`).

### tako_contents
Fetch the real content behind one result URL from `tako_search` / `tako_answer` — the rows behind a Tako card (CSV by default, or JSON), or a web page's full text. It is the step after search when you need the full data to compute over or quote; a search result carries only a preview and a chart, not its rows. One URL per call.

Precondition (Tako cards): a card is exportable only if its result carried a `content` attribute (non-null). If `content` is missing or null this call fails — use the card's preview/chart instead. Presence is necessary but not sufficient: the export gate can still refuse a rare card (a self-correcting 403 — fall back, don't retry). Web URLs always work.

Parameters:
- `url` (string, required): The result URL to fetch — a Tako card's `webpage_url`, or a web-result URL.
- `content_format` (string, optional): Tako cards only — serialization of the data: `csv` (default, text in `data`), `json_records` (row objects in `records`), or `json_compact` (compact columns+rows in `dataset`). Ignored for web URLs (always text).
- `max_rows` (integer, 1-2000, optional): Tako cards only — max rows to return. Omit for the free 20-row default; raise up to 2,000 for a larger (priced) export. Ignored for web URLs (always full text).
- `mode` (string, "inline" | "url", default "inline"): Delivery only, not row count — `inline` returns the data in the response so you can read it; `url` returns a short-lived presigned `download_url` to the same file.

### tako_graph_search
Resolve a name to Tako data-graph node ids — to see what data Tako has, and to pin (`node_ids`) into `tako_search` / `tako_answer`. Free and fast. Resolve one kind per call — a thing (`types: "entity"`) or a measure (`types: "metric"`). Results are popularity-ordered; read each node's `subtype`/`label`/`description` to pick the right one. To see an entity's data, resolve it here then call `tako_graph_related` on its id.

Parameters:
- `q` (string, required): Search text (min 2 chars).
- `types` (string, "entity" | "metric", optional): Resolve a thing ("entity") or a measure ("metric"); omit to search both — but decide up front, don't mix the two in one call.
- `label` (string, optional): NER label to prefer — a boost, not a filter. Supply it when you can categorize the term (company→ORG, country→GPE, person→PERSON, metric→METRIC, …).
- `infer_label` (boolean, optional, default true): Auto-detect the label from `q`.
- `limit` (integer, 1-50, default 20): Max results.

### tako_graph_related
Explore what a resolved graph node connects to — the map of what data Tako has for it. Free. Drilling `relation: "metrics"` returns only that node's metrics group — the smallest, cheapest view of its coverage; the overview (`node_id` alone) also returns entities, siblings, and named edges (`rel:*` like `rel:competes_with`) at more tokens. A listed metric is table-level evidence, not proof — `tako_search` is the final validator. Empty `items` is a normal answer: report the gap instead of silently falling back to web.

Parameters:
- `node_id` (string, required): Node id from `tako_graph_search` or a card's `nodes`.
- `relation` (string, optional): Relation key to page — metrics, entities, siblings, part_of, members, or rel:<phrase>. Omit for the overview.
- `q` (string, optional): Case-insensitive substring filter on name+aliases — one string per call; for several name-variants of a metric ("revenue", "sales"), call once per variant.
- `label` (string, optional) / `infer_label` (boolean, optional): NER-label preference, as in `tako_graph_search`.
- `cursor` (string, optional) / `limit` (integer, 1-100, default 50): Pagination within a drilled relation.

### tako_graph_node
Opt-in tool — off by default; enable with `?tools=graph_node` on the endpoint URL (see Connecting). Get full detail for one graph-node `id` — name, aliases, subtype, label, description. Use it when you hold a bare node id (e.g. from a `tako_search` card's `nodes`, which carry only id/name/type) and need more to compose a grounded query or confirm what it is.

Parameters:
- `id` (string, required): Opaque public node id.

### tako_visualize
Opt-in tool — off by default; enable with `?tools=visualize` on the endpoint URL (see Connecting; already on by default for ChatGPT). Create an embeddable Tako card from your OWN structured data (not from search), backed by Tako's Thin-Viz API. Provide one or more typed components; the card auto-renders inline as a chart and returns share/embed URLs.

Parameters:
- `components` (array, required): One or more `{ component_type, config, component_variant? }` objects. `component_type` is one of: header, generic_timeseries, categorical_bar, choropleth, data_table_chart, histogram, pie, table, financial_boxes, timeline, treemap, heatmap, marimekko, boxplot, waterfall, sankey, scatter, bubble, top_level_metric, person_card. `config` holds that type's data (validated server-side). The optional `component_variant` string selects a type variant (e.g. 'simple', 'financial'). `person_card` must be the only component.
- `title` (string, optional): Card title
- `description` (string, optional): Card description
- `source` (string, optional): Data source attribution shown in the footer
- `height` (integer, 100-2000, optional): Chart height in pixels
- `normalize_currencies` (string, optional): Target ISO 4217 code to convert currency-denominated datasets

### tako_agent
Opt-in tool — off by default; enable with `?tools=agent` on the endpoint URL (see Connecting). Run Tako's Answer Agent for open-ended, multi-step questions whose shape needs figuring out — cohorts, ranking or filtering by criteria, aggregation, and multi-hop reasoning across many entities; also the fallback when `tako_search` / `tako_answer` return nothing. Returns a synthesized answer plus supporting chart cards (~30–90s). On ChatGPT, exposed as the `tako_agent_start` / `tako_agent_wait` pair to fit the host's tool-call timeout model.

Parameters:
- `query` (string, required): The open-ended, analytical question.
- `sources` (array, optional): both by default (`["data","web"]`); pass `["data"]` for connected data only or `["web"]` for open-web search only. (`"tako"` is a legacy synonym for `"data"`.)
- `thread_id` (string UUID, optional): Continue a prior agent run's thread as a follow-up; omit to start a new thread.

### get_credit_balance
Opt-in tool — off by default; enable with `?tools=credits` on the endpoint URL (see Connecting). Check the connected account's API credit balance.

Parameters: none.
